column2: The Far East

In the throes of The Event, the Mighty Dragon of the East, the illustrious Middle Kingdom of China was turnt tumult in the cacophony of unrest which left the periphery of its mighty reach to extend their designs across the Western Regions. From high above in Himalayas, kingdom across the peaks and valleys via for influence over the golden urn, as holy representatives of the Lamas of old dispute long and bitterly over who holds the center in the great mandala of Dharma Lords. While in the Valley of the Tarim as great Oasis Kingdoms form the sinews between the East and West of the Old Continent tempered only by the stampede of great horse lords who sally forth from their plain homes in the name of the Eternal Khan or the sword of the flaming prophet.
The Subcontinent

The Indian Subcontinent, home to a multitude of peoples and beliefs that stretch to the misty era of myths and legends. The peoples of these lands have seen great conquerers, sage-kings and peacemakers leave marks that ripple across time. Even after The Event not much has change about that song and dance. In the centuries prior the Mighty Empires like that of Khalasa and the Deccan fought great wars that rock the heart of the continent only to leave but the echoes of that conflict upon the still surface of the reflective surface of one's soul. For that soul there are many communities and paths to walk for in the waning years of your youth as the blade grows heavy will you find the answers you seek in the hymns of Old. A hidden truth that might be the necessary change that will leave a raging tide in your wake.
The Muslim World

Long ago, The heart of the Jamaah al-Islam was forged not only the blade but the wise rule of the Caliphs of Old. Though that glorious era has long since passed to the descendants of those that heeded the word of the Prophet (PBUH) have carried the Quran through the tumult of The Event itself. In this new era of chaos where the Ghazi warriors fight for what they see as just, others seek answer with the divine be they Christians, Jews or others that believe in the glory and light of his many names. In the temporal realm leaders navigate the intrigue of the court just as much as those fought in the field vying to be the center of world's attention in the eras to come.
Eastern Europe

A crossroads between Europe and Asia, the lands of Eastern Europe have long been tumultuous and everchanging in fortunes. Dynasties that once stood proud have been replaced time and again by usurpers, and faiths from every corner have been made to cooperate with one another. The Russians quarrel among themselves as to which faith truly has the right to reform Russia, while the Carpathian kingdoms of Hungary and Romania are host to dynastic disputes and religious tensions. Poland, the Baltics, and Ruthenia stand ready against outside incursion, intending to never again be the stomping grounds of other empires.
Western Europe

Long has the days of Empire and Glory been the stuff of legends myths and folklore for the peoples of the Old Continent. Waning in its years the Mighty Empire of Europa once claimed dominion over all of the continent as a symbol of the ancient promise of Liberty and Fraternity, a community for all that basked in the untold peace it brought. The Old Order while weak still hold to the keys to power be it the Emperor in Brussels or the Pope in Rome, change seems to be in the air again having once been but murmurs in the dark corners of society a glorious revolution will be the spring glow to revitalize the stagnancy that has griped the land.
Hendrik Coudenhove

A young ruler elected from one of Europa's many prominent families, Hendrik is eager to prove himself and guide the empire to prosperity. However, keeping his throne is dependant on appeasing and curtailing the powerful vassals who are always at risk of plunging Europa into civil war, having done so multiple times. With enemies within and without, Henrik must play a balancing act lest he lose everything.
Edwin FitzSpatstone

Great Britain managed to re-assemble itself in the 25th century under Thelema conquerors, though the current Kingdom of Britain is now ruled by the Glorian-adhering FitzSpatstones. Prince Edwin is faced with a divided Britannia, as the Scottish and the Irish fervently maintain their independence while the ancient capital of London is held by a vassal republic that took it by force. With heartland Britain religiously and culturally divided, Edwin must overcome adversity for Britain to once again rule the waves.
Steffen Stromer

Bavaria stands as Catholicism's northern bulwark, ever a mighty kingdom intended to rival and curtail heathen Europa. However, the young King Steffen has increasingly found his relationship with the Vatican to be tenuous, being an openly gay cynic who is more concerned with architectural projects than his pious duty. Despite this, Steffen is also an ambitious man who may find benefit to staying in the Papacy's good graces, were he to expand further into Germany.
Georges Colonna-Walewski

Few cities are as heavily contested in Europe as Paris, which has found itself deflecting would-be conquerors time and again. Despite his illegitimate birth and lowborn origins, Georges carved out a semblance of order for his Parisian Republic and proved to be a ruthless yet capable leader. Paris is once again surrounded by enemies on all sides, and Georges must bring forth all that the Republic has to muster if he is to keep the Jacobin dream alive.
Gionna Agnesi

King Francesco of Lumbardia has been murdered on the orders of the Doge of Venice, and now Francesco's widow Gionna sits on the Lumbardian throne. In the ever-shifting tide of schemes and ambitions that have long shaped Italian politics, Gionna intends to bring fire and fury upon the Venetians for what they took from her. Northern Italy is bracing for a bloodbath, and such a spark may be what's needed for Lumbardia to assert dominance across the Peninsula.
Piotr Puttkamer

Pomerania is a realm gaining a foothold in Eastern Europe, so long as it can keep its momentum. Piotr recently vassalized the High Chiefdom of Lubusz and has greater ambitions to expand into Poland and Ossiland alike, ready to stand as a champion of the Mariavite Church. However, his realm is in turn threatened by the Chronicler heathens of Brandenburg, his chief obstacle to a mighty Pomerania.
Edgars Ozols

Among the most powerful Christian realms in Europe, the Baltic Empire stands today as a bastion and prime influence of Lutheran Protestantism. However, it has also faced great instability and strife as House Ozols only recently brought the Empire back to a single-dynasty succession. Keizars Edgars must take care that his empire not fall apart, whether at the hands of outside infidels or inside traitors.
Taran Djakov

Once a peasant from a lowborn family, Taran led a Proletkult uprising to take the holy city of Petrograd and create a communal republic. Surrounded by Christians on every side from Lutheran to Orthodox, it is now Taran's responsibility to spread the revolution all the way to Moskva, and restore Russia as a realm of the people.
Csanád Fehérlófi

Descended from the White Mare King who overthrew the Coronist rulers of Hungary, Csanád II now rules the kingdom as a Népmese pagan realm. There still exist pockets of Coronist holdouts, including one vassal from the old House Kinizsi who holds the Crown of Saint Stephen from Csanád, while other Christian vassals grow uneasy with their pagan king. Csanád's youngest son is set to inherit as dictated by the faith's Ultimogeniture traditions, but a steady hand must ensure that Hungary remains strong.
Alexandru Dragescu

Since the last Emperor of Romania died without an heir, the remaining lands are being fought over between two cousins of the once-ruling House Dragescu. Alexandru holds the old imperial capital of Bucharest, though his cousin Vladimir carries the Iron Crown and an equally legitimate claim to the Romanian throne. Alexandru must act fast to secure his claim and reunite Romania, for a throne can only be sat upon by a single Emperor.
Satwant Kharak-Singh

The Sikhs and their Empire of Khalasa has ruled Punjab and much of northern India. The Deccan War destroyed the Sikhs' offensive capabilities, and Khalasa has receded to Punjab. Now, Satwant looks to defend his people and perhaps replicate the military triumphs of his ancestors. North India is now in anarchy... a double-edged sword for the Sikhs.
Syed Ali-Khan

Bengal stands as a great power in Southeast Asia, a Muslim powerhouse in a sea of Hindus and other non-believers. The empire rules the mouth of the Ganges, and Bengal has ambitions for the rest of India, especially following the collapse of Khalasa. Syed, Shahanshah of Bengal, is aging, but he still has the drive to conquer as many other mujahidin in the history of Bengal and India as a whole.
Freida Lotlikar

A young woman whose family is steeped in tragedy, Freida is a lamb in a land of wolves. The Republic of Mumbai may be a place where open warfare is more rare, but it is nonetheless full of cutthroat politics and spectacle. Freida sometimes wishes life could be like Masala Rasa, but she does not live in that world.
Munni Devi

Central India has long been a battleground, and the people have suffered for it greatly. The Bundelis in particular suffered under the rules of Sikhs and Muslim conquerors, but it was Munni Devi who had enough. The warrior-queen led dalits and tribes in a rebellion against the Sikhs, and Munni has established herself as a powerful ruler ever since.
Tissahamy Morane

The Maharaja of Lanka is neither Sinhala nor Tamil, but Vedda. Tisahammy Morane comes from the ancient Morane clan who claim descent from the Yakkha Queen Kiriamma also known as Kuveni who supported Prince Vijaya, founder of the Sinhala state. The Morane clan has largely dominated Vedda politics following the Event, eventually dominating the politics of the island. Tisahammy must balance the interests of Sinhalas and Tamils, neither of which trust him or his clan.
Barquq el-Tawfik

The Egyptian Empire arose from the ashes of the event under the legendary Abdel Hakim el-Gamal, a general whose cult of an-Nahar aimed to restore Egypt to its former glory, in hope of one day bringing about the new day. The last Emperor of Egypt, a Muslim named Hakim el-Tawfik, groomed his nephew Barquq to rule, but Hakim's generals cause the empire to collapse into civil war after he disappeared on a pilgrimage. Now, Barquq rules a rump state in Aswan, but he looks to reclaim to glory of the empire: his claim is still true.
Mohammad Borumand

Iran has always been a land of diverse people and faiths, but Twelver Shi'ism remains the dominant religion with the mullahs having great power in many realms in the area. Mohammad Borumand, Wali of Tehran, is beloved by his people and the mullahs. While being a kind man, he is no fool and he knows of the threats looming around him from both sectarians and co-religionists.
Uzi Ben-Avi

Since the Event, the Holy Land has been through a lot: divided into petty city-states, dominated by foreign empires, and occasionally experiencing brief spells of united rule under Tzabar or Filastini Rulers. Since the retreat of Egypt, Tel Avi has fallen into the hands of Uzi Ben-Avi, descended from a side branch of the Ben Yehuda dynasty, whose founder Elazar briefly united Israel as an independent kingdom, and whose progeny mostly continued his passion for scholarly and religious pursuits rather than his ambitions of rulership, with many serving as Rishon LeTzion in the past. Uzi however, is clever and deceitful, a dangerous player with aims for power.
Majdi Al-Saud

Arabia, the heart of Islam, still holds great importance in the heart of all Muslims. However, the once resplendent House al-Saud has fallen in ruin following the Event: the very Salafists the Saudis funded destroyed Saudi Arabia. Majdi Al-Saud, a scion of House al-Saud, stands against the grind of history, fighting back against the Salafists who overthrew them.
Atilla Günesh

In recent memory, one ruler came close to claiming the heartland of Anatolia for himself: Atilla Günesh, the old lion, who once controlled most of Cappadocia and the Toros mountains. Nevertheless, his imperial ambitions for the whole of Turkey were smashed at the Battle of Kahraman, where a hastily formed coalition broke the back of Atilla's army and slew his two favorite sons. Now, none of the remaining princes seem ready to take on their father's mantle, and his numerous descendants have already begun to squabble amongst themselves.
Mönkhbat Hu

Blue-skied Mongolia has become a land of steppes and hordes once again. Mönkhbat, the old wolf, gained Ulaanbaatar by killing his hated relative by chasing him deep into the mountains where it is said that he either fell to his death or that Mönkhbat choked him to death with the string of his bow. Being a direct descendant of the sublime lord Genghis has brought him a great deal of respect with all Mongols, but his raids and battles have brought him even more. There are only a few in the steppe who can claim to be his equal.
Löntsen Aglen

Despite China's influence retreating east, Tibet has remained divided. The various Buddhist schools, mainly the Yellow Hats, Red Hats, and the matriachal Ngochulgspa, have remained divided after the contentious re-emergence of the 15th Dalai Lama. Löntsen Aglen unified Ü-Tsa, and he is the most powerful warlord in Tibet currently. However, he is old, and Lhasa is still held by the Ngochulgspa: any conquest of Tibet will not be complete without Lhasa.
Bufang Han

The Western Protectorate has only recently been restored by the Hong: a distant island of influence by China. Han emissaries being sent forth to re-establish contact with the Western Barbarians that once connected China to the wider world and Bufang Han being one of the highest officials sent with the mandate of the Dragon Throne of the East. Will he stay loyal to the Distant Empire, or will he embrace ambition to forge his own destiny?
Amanni Nafisi

The Uighurs have long inhabited the Tarim Basin, and they have historically existed as independent states or were controlled by many civilizations including China, the Mongols, the Tibetans, and various Turkic peoples. Amanni Nafisi came to power in a rare circumstance: a kind female musician who is beloved by her people. However, the arrival of the Western Protectorate poses a new threat: can Amanni protect her people from another great power?
Erjene Maria Klyonov

The Kingdom of Irkutsk, ruled by Buryats, was long a stronghold of Christianity in Siberia, a bridge between European Russia and the Russian Far East. However, Irkutsk was raided by Narmandakh Gelenkhüü, and the kingdom collapsed. Erjene Maria Klyonov rules what is left of Irkutsk, steadfast against Khanists and any other raiders. She hopes to one day restore Irkutsk to greatness: this would be a hard task to realize.
